text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The government agreed at its weekend meeting on the composition of the teams which will negotiate loans with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. The teams include the finance and economic reform ministers, as well as the central bank governor.
ADEVARUL

- National Bank governor Mugur Isarescu told private television ProTV he expected prices to go up by around 30 percent in the next few months, also under the impact of pending rises in the price of electricity.
- Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said he expected managers of the State Ownership Fund to be replaced by the end of the month on inaccurate management so far.
AZI
- Banca Internationala a Religiilor SA said it planned to increase its capital by 25 billion lei to 75 billion and also to attract credit lines from abroad.
ZIUA
- The government ratified a loan accord between Romania and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the rehabilitation of roads.
LIBERTATEA
- The CEC plans to raise interest rates on deposits starting next month. The Banca Comerciala Romana SA rose rates on leu deposits starting Monday.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Outstanding debts to the Romanian Oil Company amount to 45.5 billion lei, of which 11 billion owed by farming units.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies opened an extraordinary session on Monday to discuss delayed draft laws.
- Former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) held an extraordinary national conference when it elected former President Ion Iliescu as its chairman.
- Coal miners in the Jiu Valley staged a meeting at the weekend in favour of union leader Miron Cozma, detained earlier this month for allegedly undermining state authority.
ADEVARUL
- Foreigners adopted 1,770 Romanian children in 1996, 13 times more than in 1992, the Romanian Adoption Committee said.
- Valerian Stan, head of the Prime Minister's control department, says in an interview his department receives a daily 20 complaints against corruption.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Jiu Valley coal miners threaten to come to Bucharest unless Cozma is released from prison during investigations.
- The Socialist Labour Party, the Greater Romania Party, the Socialist Party and the Romanian National Unity Party refuse to acknowledge PDSR chairman Iliescu as opposition leader.
- An overcroded tramway turned over in the eastern city of Iasi killing two and wounding more than 40.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A newspaper poll shows Romanians agree the fight against corruption is a priority.
LIBERTATEA
- The government approved new norms for the application of the law on restitution of nationalised houses, which are favourable to former ownwers, the newspaper says.
COTIDIANUL
- Interim state television general manager Stere Gulea says in an interview the station's newly employed workers are people who understand the current difficult times. ($=5,016 lei)
